title: SSH Brute Force by Source IP — High Severity (Level >= 10)
source: Wazuh docs: rule reference (rule 5763, 5712, 5720)
description: Hunts for high-severity SSH brute-force alerts triggered by Wazuh's correlation engine, returning all events where multiple authentication failures from a single source IP exceeded the threshold in the last 24 hours.

title: SSH Authentication Failures by Source IP (Aggregated)
source: Wazuh indexer API docs: use case — top risky users aggregation
description: Aggregates SSH authentication failure alerts in the last hour, returning the top source IPs by count to identify active brute-force campaigns.

title: Failed Logins Targeting Root / Admin Accounts
source: Wazuh docs: threat hunting authentication failures; derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds all authentication failure events targeting privileged accounts (root, admin, Administrator) across the last 24 hours, useful for detecting focused credential attacks against high-value accounts.

title: Windows Failed Logons (Event ID 4625) by Source IP
source: Wazuh rule 60122 (Windows auth failure); wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub
description: Searches for all Windows Event ID 4625 (failed logon) records ingested by Wazuh agents in the last 24 hours, providing a baseline for brute-force and password spraying detection on Windows endpoints.

title: Windows Successful Logons (Event ID 4624) with Logon Type
source: mtask.github.io: Query and analyze Wazuh indexer data with Python (2024)
description: Returns successful Windows logon events (4624) while excluding service logons (type 5), allowing hunting for interactive (type 2), network (type 3), and remote interactive (type 10) logons that may indicate lateral movement.

title: Sudo Execution Alerts — All Sudo-Related Activity
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux privilege escalation techniques with Wazuh
description: Hunts for all sudo-related alerts triggered by Wazuh, including successful and failed sudo invocations, to identify unauthorized privilege escalation attempts across monitored endpoints.

title: Sudo Execution with Sensitive Binaries (GTFOBins-Relevant)
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux privilege escalation techniques (GTFOBins pattern)
description: Finds sudo commands that invoked binaries commonly abused for privilege escalation (GTFOBins-listed tools like bash, python, vim, find, etc.) in the last 7 days, surfacing potentially malicious sudo abuse.

title: SUID/SGID Bit Changes — File Integrity Monitoring
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches FIM (syscheck) alerts for files whose permissions contain a setuid/setgid bit (indicated by 's' in permissions), flagging new or modified SUID/SGID binaries that may have been planted for privilege escalation.

title: Privileged Group Modification — /etc/group, /etc/sudoers FIM Hits
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux privilege escalation techniques (T1098.007)
description: Detects FIM changes to critical privilege-control files: /etc/group, /etc/gshadow, /etc/sudoers, and /etc/sudoers.d/*, alerting when an attacker adds a user to the sudo/wheel group or modifies sudoers configuration.

title: Root-Level Command Execution — Rule Level 12+
source: Wazuh indexer API GitHub discussion #37771
description: Returns all highest-severity (level 12+) alerts in the last 24 hours, which typically include privilege escalation, critical system compromise indicators, and active-response triggers.

title: SSH Authorized Keys — File Addition or Modification
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1098.004)
description: Finds FIM alerts for any authorized_keys file added or modified across monitored endpoints in the last 7 days, a primary indicator of SSH key-based persistence.

title: SSH Configuration File Modifications — sshd_config
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1098.004)
description: Finds FIM alerts for changes to /etc/ssh/sshd_config across the last 30 days, catching attackers who enable PermitRootLogin, PubkeyAuthentication, or otherwise weaken SSH configuration for persistence.

title: Cron Job Creation — New Files in /etc/cron.* Directories
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1053.003); Elastic detection-rules repo
description: Hunts for newly added files (syscheck event=added) in cron directories across the last 7 days, detecting scheduled-task persistence via cron job creation.

title: Systemd Timer/Service Unit File Creation or Modification
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1053.006); Elastic detection-rules repo (systemd timers)
description: Detects FIM events on systemd service/timer directories, flagging creation or modification of unit files that may establish persistent execution via systemd timers or services.

title: New User Account Creation — Windows Event ID 4720
source: Wazuh rule 60103 (custom); wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub (rule 100005)
description: Searches for Windows Event ID 4720 (user account created) across the last 30 days, detecting unauthorized local account creation for persistence on Windows endpoints.

title: RC Script Modification — /etc/rc.local FIM Alert
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1037.004)
description: Finds FIM alerts for modifications to /etc/rc.local, an older but still-viable boot-time persistence mechanism that executes commands during system startup.

title: Shell Profile Modifications — .bashrc, .profile, .bash_profile FIM
source: Wazuh blog: Detecting common Linux persistence techniques (T1546.004)
description: Finds FIM alerts for shell profile file modifications (.bashrc, .profile, .zshrc) across monitored endpoints, detecting Unix shell configuration modification as a stealth persistence technique.

title: Windows Process Creation — Event ID 4688 (All)
source: Wazuh rule 60103/67027; Google Groups Wazuh community
description: Returns all Windows process creation events (Event ID 4688) in the last 24 hours, providing a baseline for anomaly hunting in process ancestry and command-line arguments.

title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
source: Wazuh rule 67027; wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub (rule 100002) T1059.001
description: Hunts for PowerShell processes invoked with -EncodedCommand or -enc flags, indicating obfuscated command execution commonly used in fileless malware and living-off-the-land attacks.

title: PowerShell Download Cradle Detection
source: Wazuh rule 67027; wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub (rule 100003) T1105
description: Detects PowerShell download cradles (DownloadString, DownloadFile, Invoke-WebRequest, Net.WebClient) in command lines, indicating potential malware staging or payload retrieval.

title: Office Applications Spawning Shell Processes
source: Wazuh rule 67027; wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub (rule 100004) T1566.001
description: Finds process creation events where Microsoft Office applications spawned a shell process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe), a strong indicator of macro-based malware delivery.

title: Reverse Shell Indicators — Suspicious Process Command Lines
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches full_log for common reverse-shell command patterns (netcat with -e, bash /dev/tcp, Python/perl socket backdoors), indicating successful exploitation and callback.

title: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Relationships (Linux)
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches full_log for suspicious piped command patterns where download utilities (wget/curl) pipe directly to shell interpreters, a common staging technique for malware and scripts.

title: FIM Changes in Sensitive Directories — /etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin
source: Wazuh FIM documentation; Google Groups Wazuh community
description: Hunts for FIM events in critical system directories (/etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin) in the last 48 hours, surfacing potential tampering with system binaries or configuration files.

title: FIM Events in Web Server Directories — Web Shell Detection
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds FIM alerts in common web server directories, identifying newly added or modified files that could be web shells uploaded by attackers for persistent remote access.

title: FIM Events — Executable Files Added Outside Package Manager Paths
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Hunts for files added to world-writable directories (/tmp, /dev/shm, /var/tmp) in the last 48 hours, often used by attackers to stage executables and scripts outside of package-manager-controlled paths.

title: FIM Deletion Events — File Removed (Possible Evidence Cleanup)
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds FIM deletion events in /var/log, /root, and /home directories, surfacing potential anti-forensic activity where attackers delete log files or evidence after compromise.

title: Alerts from External (Non-RFC1918) Source IPs
source: Wazuh dashboard threat hunting guide; mintlify.app Wazuh docs
description: Finds all alerts in the last 24 hours where the source IP is not a private/RFC1918 address, surfacing attacks originating from the public internet rather than internal lateral movement.

title: Top External Source IPs by Alert Volume (Aggregated)
source: Wazuh indexer API docs: use case — fetch unique source IPs
description: Aggregates the top 20 non-RFC1918 source IPs by alert count in the last 24 hours, helping security analysts quickly identify external actors generating the most alert noise.

title: Suricata / Network IDS Alerts — Rule Group Match
source: Wazuh integration: Suricata; socfortress/Wazuh-Rules GitHub
description: Returns all Suricata IDS alerts in the last 24 hours sorted by severity, providing visibility into network-based threat detections from Wazuh's Suricata integration.

title: High-Volume Outbound Connections — Sysmon Network Events
source: Wazuh rule groups: sysmon_event_3 (Sysmon network connection); socfortress/Wazuh-Rules
description: Finds Sysmon Event ID 3 (network connection) events ingested by Wazuh in the last 24 hours, enabling hunting for unusual outbound connections, C2 beaconing, or data exfiltration.

title: Log Tampering — Auditd Service Stop or Syslog Restart
wazuh: {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"bool": {"should": [{"wildcard": {"full_log": "*auditd*stop*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*auditd*terminat*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*systemctl stop auditd*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*service auditd stop*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*systemctl stop rsyslog*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*systemctl stop syslog*"}}, {"wildcard": {"full_log": "*systemctl disable auditd*"}}], "minimum_should_match": 1}}, {"range": {"timestamp": {"gte": "now-30d"}}}]}}}
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches full_log for commands that stop or disable the auditd/rsyslog/syslog services, a common defense evasion technique to blind monitoring before malicious activity.

title: Windows Event Log Clearing — Event ID 1102
source: Wazuh Windows event channel; derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds Windows Security Event Log cleared events (Event ID 1102) in the last 30 days, a strong indicator of anti-forensic activity where an attacker attempts to erase their tracks.

title: Firewall Rule Modification — iptables/nftables Changes
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds log entries showing iptables or nftables firewall rule modifications, which may indicate an attacker reconfiguring the host firewall to allow C2 traffic or disable defenses.

title: Malware Detection — Rootcheck, VirusTotal, Yara Alerts
source: Wazuh dashboard built-in Malware Detection filter; Google Groups Wazuh community
description: Returns all alerts from Wazuh's malware detection modules (rootcheck, VirusTotal integration, Yara) in the last 7 days, providing a consolidated view of potential malware and IOC hits.

title: Windows Alternate Logon — Event ID 4648 (Explicit Credentials)
source: cas-cyber.gitbook.io: lateral movement detection with Wazuh
description: Finds Windows Event ID 4648 (logon with explicit credentials) events, which indicate a process used alternate credentials — commonly seen with PsExec, runas, and other lateral movement tools.

title: Windows Scheduled Task Creation — Event ID 4698
source: Wazuh rule 60103 (custom); ronakmishra28/wazuh-enterprise-siem-lab GitHub
description: Searches for Windows Event ID 4698 (scheduled task created) across monitored endpoints, used both for persistence and lateral movement via scheduled task execution on remote systems.

title: SSH Connections from Unusual Source Hosts (Last 24h Aggregation)
source: Wazuh indexer API docs: aggregation patterns
description: Aggregates SSH-related alerts by agent name (source host) in the last 24 hours, identifying systems that are generating unusual volumes of SSH traffic potentially indicative of lateral movement.

title: Web Attack Patterns — SQLi, XSS, Web Attack Group Alerts
source: Wazuh dashboard threat hunting guide: web attack patterns
description: Returns all alerts from Wazuh's web attack detection groups (attack, sqli, xss, web) in the last 24 hours, covering web application attacks detected by the Wazuh ruleset.

title: System Discovery Commands — Reconnaissance in Full Logs
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches full_log for common system and network discovery commands (whoami, ifconfig, netstat, systeminfo, net user, etc.), flagging reconnaissance activity that often precedes lateral movement.

title: Vulnerability Detection — Specific CVE Search
source: Wazuh indexer API docs: use case — vulnerability detection (CVE search)
description: Searches the Wazuh vulnerabilities index for a specific CVE (example: CVE-2020-14393) to identify which monitored endpoints are affected, enabling targeted patching.

title: SCA (Security Configuration Assessment) Failures — CIS Benchmark Misses
source: Wazuh SCA module documentation; diagonalciso/soc-ops GitHub (CIS category)
description: Returns all level-7 SCA (Security Configuration Assessment) alerts in the last 7 days, identifying endpoints that failed CIS benchmarks or other compliance checks.

title: High Severity Alert Triage — Level 10+ with MITRE ATT&CK Mapping
source: Wazuh indexer API GitHub discussion #37771 (adapted)
description: Returns all high-severity (level >= 10) alerts with MITRE ATT&CK mappings in the last 24 hours, providing security analysts a prioritized triage list with key fields for rapid investigation.

title: Alerts by MITRE ATT&CK Tactic — Credential Access Focus
source: Wazuh MITRE ATT&CK mapping docs; opennix.org Wazuh indexer API guide
description: Hunts for all alerts tagged with the MITRE ATT&CK Credential Access tactic in the last 7 days, covering brute-force, credential dumping, and password theft techniques.

title: Alerts by MITRE ATT&CK Technique — T1547 (Boot/Logon Autostart Execution)
source: Wazuh MITRE ATT&CK mapping docs; mintlify.app Wazuh threat hunting guide
description: Returns all alerts mapped to MITRE technique T1547 (Boot or Logon Autostart Execution), covering registry run keys, startup folders, and other auto-start persistence mechanisms on Windows and Linux.

title: All MITRE ATT&CK-Mapped Alerts — Past 24 Hours
source: Wazuh MITRE ATT&CK mapping docs
description: Returns all alerts that have MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs mapped in the last 24 hours, useful for a broad hunt across all mapped adversary behaviors sorted by severity.

source: socfortress/Wazuh-Rules GitHub (Sysmon integration); socfortress/CoPilot-Search-Queries (lsass_memory_access.yaml)
description: Finds Sysmon Event ID 10 (process access) events, which are used to detect LSASS memory access — a primary technique for credential dumping tools like Mimikatz.

title: Windows Security Audit Policy Change — Event ID 4719
source: Wazuh Windows event channel; derived pattern, no single source
description: Searches for Windows Event ID 4719 (system audit policy was changed), which may indicate an attacker modifying audit settings to reduce logging before conducting malicious activity.

title: Windows Service Creation — Event ID 7045 (System Log)
source: Wazuh Windows event channel; derived pattern, no single source
description: Finds Windows Event ID 7045 (new service installed) in the last 7 days, detecting potential persistence or lateral movement via service creation on remote systems.

title: High-Risk Users — Top Accounts by Alert Association
source: Wazuh indexer API docs: use case — identify most risky users
description: Aggregates the top 15 users (data.dstuser) associated with triggered alerts in the last 7 days, identifying accounts that appear most frequently in security events for risk scoring.

title: Rule ID — SSH Brute Force Correlation (Rule 5763)
source: Wazuh docs: rule 5763 (sshd brute force correlation); amvatlabs.com SSH brute-force detection blog
description: Returns all alerts generated by Wazuh rule 5763 (SSH brute force detected) in the last 24 hours, the rule that correlates multiple authentication failures from the same source IP.

title: Agent Disconnection — Detecting Silenced Monitored Endpoints
source: Wazuh rule groups: agent connection events
description: Finds Wazuh agent-related alerts in the last hour, including agent disconnection events that may indicate an attacker disabling monitoring on a compromised endpoint.

title: All High-Severity Alerts (Level >= 12) Without MITRE Mapping
source: derived pattern, no single source
description: Returns top-50 high-severity (level >= 12) alerts without MITRE ATT&CK mappings in the last 72 hours, helping identify gaps in ATT&CK coverage for critical security events.
